items.statement: Final: opposite effects of the coordination environment on the two half-reactions
items.expected: Finally, integrate actual reaction-state, family-comparison and resting-state results to explain that the NN tricarbonyl favors alcohol oxidation, whereas the NNS dicarbonyl can favor ketone reduction through the S channel. Comparison of effective oxidation barriers supports alcohol oxidation as the slower half-cycle within these candidate models. Make an explicit computationally supported choice/explanation; merely listing candidates or trends is insufficient. Do not infer a uniquely true active species, actual populations or precise rates.

items.statement: Final: configuration-dependent preference and its ensemble implications
items.expected: Finally, infer from actual paired structures/energies and mirror-image relationships that a fixed catalyst configuration can produce an S/R difference and that its mirror image corresponds to the opposite product mapping. Results for a single configuration with achiral ligands cannot establish experimental macroscopic ee. Support this ensemble interpretation with actual mappings and comparisons; a generic statement that there are limitations is insufficient. Additional determination of actual configuration populations or the complete mirror-image reaction network is not required.
